caption:
I’m about to tell you something most people are too scared to admit:

You don’t have a talent problem.
You don’t have a luck problem.
You have a HUNGER problem.

See, while you’re scrolling through Instagram at 11pm wondering why you’re not rich yet... some kid in his garage is making his 47th sales call of the day.

While you’re “networking” at happy hour... someone else is studying, practicing, bleeding to get better.

While you’re waiting for the “right time”.
.. your competition is TAKING what they want.

Here’s the truth nobody wants to hear:
Success has a price tag. Always has. Always will.
Strained relationships. Missed parties. Lonely nights. Brutal mornings. That’s the invoice.

Most people see that price and say “too expensive.”
Winners pull out their wallet and ask “where do I sign?”

In sales (hell, in LIFE), I’ve watched this movie a thousand times. The guy who makes one more call at 6pm drives a different car than the guy who clocks out at 5.

It’s not complicated. It’s just uncomfortable.

So here’s your homework:
What are you willing to sacrifice RIGHT NOW that your broke friends won’t?
Can’t answer? Then stop complaining about your bank account.
Find your hunger or stay poor.
Your move,

author: Angela Soko | High Ticket Sales
transcript: Oh, you have to want it more than everyone else, not just a little more, not I'll try when I feel like it. I'm talking about an obsession that looks fucking insane to a normal person. While they're sleeping, you're working. While they're celebrating small wins, you're hunting the next one. When they quit because it hurts, you push harder because giving up on what you actually want hurts more. This isn't about talent. Talent is bullshit. This isn't about luck. Luck is what losers call hard work. This is about hunger, a hunger so deep it consumes everything. Your thoughts, your actions, every decision you make. It's about wanting something so badly you're willing to sacrifice something most people won't. Endure what weak people can't. Attempt what scared people don't dare. And of course, there's a price. You lose relationships. People won't understand you. You'll miss moments that you could never really get back ever. But that's the test. If those obstacles stop you, you don't want it enough. Someone else wants it more. Someone else bled more, risked more, gave more. In sales, you see this daily. The rep who goes home at 5 p.m. versus the one who makes one more call. Guess which one's buying rental property after rental property while the other one's still asking permission to take a day off. So ask yourself, what are you willing to give up? What comfort can you sacrifice? What pain can you endure? Because you can't answer that. You've already lost. Find your hunger or stay broke.
title: Find Your Hunger or Stay Broke
one_liner: Success demands obsessive sacrifice — talent and luck matter less than relentless hunger.
key_points: Talent and luck are irrelevant; hunger and willingness to sacrifice are the real differentiators
While others rest or celebrate, high achievers are still grinding and hunting the next win
Success has a real price: strained relationships, missed moments, and social isolation
Ask yourself what comfort you're willing to sacrifice that others won't — if you can't answer, you've already lost
